profiles.Summary: Grim Dawn runs excellently on the Steam Deck via Proton, with the game's modest PC requirements (GTX 500 series recommended) well within the Deck's capabilities. The ARPG isometric perspective and engine are lightweight enough to sustain 60 fps at high settings with a reasonable TDP budget.
profiles.BasisNote: No specific Steam Deck player reports were available; profiles are estimated from the game's PC requirements (recommended GPU is GTX 500-series class, well below the Deck's RDNA 2 GPU) and the game's known engine characteristics. MaxBattery.Notes: Rendering at 960x600 with FSR upscaling keeps the GPU very relaxed and the 6 W TDP cap maximizes battery life. The game is perfectly playable at 30 fps for a slow-paced ARPG session.

profiles.Summary: Grim Dawn is a 2016 ARPG with modest PC requirements that the Steam Deck handles very comfortably, easily sustaining 60 fps at medium-to-high settings with TDP headroom to spare. ProtonDB reports a platinum tier with strong confidence, indicating it runs well out of the box under Proton with no major issues.
profiles.BasisNote: No Deck-specific reports were available; profiles are estimated from the game's modest 2016 PC requirements (minimum GPU roughly GTX 460 class, well below the Deck's RDNA 2) and the strong platinum ProtonDB tier. On your first run, check fps in a busy boss fight or large outdoor area — if the Optimal profile holds 55+ fps there, you can safely try Max Performance.

MaxBattery.Notes: Dropping to 40 Hz with a low TDP and FSR upscaling maximises session length; the game's top-down ARPG perspective means the lower render resolution is barely noticeable. Half-rate shading is unnecessary given the already low GPU load.

MaxPerformance.Notes: Grim Dawn's 2016 engine is well within the Deck's capabilities at full settings and 90 Hz; expect smooth gameplay even in large enemy packs, with only very heavy particle-filled encounters occasionally dipping toward 70 fps. Battery life is significantly reduced at uncapped TDP.
